podcast.body: Mellencamp considered it pretentious to write political songs before this album. The songwriting process for "Scarecrow" marked a shift, as he meticulously typed and rewrote lyrics, a departure from his previous method of simply writing them down once. This album became known for its politically charged songs like "Rain on the Scarecrow." "I typed out the lyrics I never used a typewriter before I used to just write them down on a piece of paper and never change them."

podcast.body: This 1985 LP became John Mellencamp's biggest selling album ever, generating an "unprecedented" five top 40 hits, including three top tens, and marking his imperial peak. "after his 1985 LP, Scarecrow became his biggest selling album ever generating an unprecedented five top 40 hits including three top tens."
